title: No-deleting principle for two unitary copies
abstract: Pati and Braunstein defined a deleting machine and showed the impossibility of deleting one of two identical copies of an unknown quantum state. So far, no one has defined two non-identical copies of a quantum state, of course no one has discussed the impossibility of deleting one of two non-identical copies of an unknown quantum state. In this paper, we define $u|ψ>$ and $U|ψ>$, where $u$ and $U$ are any unitary operators, as two unitary copies of a quantum state $|ψ>$, and show that it is impossible to delete one of two unitary copies of an unknown state.
summary: This paper tackles a generalization of the no-cloning theorem by examining the deletion of one copy from two non-identical unitary copies of an unknown quantum state. The authors define these copies using arbitrary unitaries $U$ and $V$ acting on $|\psiangle$. Through rigorous mathematical analysis, they prove that such a universal deletion operation is impossible.
main_problem: The paper investigates the fundamental impossibility of deleting one copy when presented with two non-identical, unknown quantum states.
main_result: It is shown that a proposed 'deleting machine' for two unitary copies of an unknown state cannot successfully delete one of them.
method: The authors analyze the action of a defined linear operator (the deleting machine) on arbitrary input states and derive mathematical contradictions based on the assumption that deletion is possible.
model_or_system: The system models two 'unitary copies' of an unknown state $|\psiangle$, represented by $U|\psiangle$ and $V|\psiangle$, where $U$ and $V$ are arbitrary unitary operators. The process is formalized using a linear operator acting on the joint Hilbert space.
key_observables: The success or failure of the deletion operation, analyzed through the structure of the resulting state in an ancilla register.
important_parameters: The unitaries $U$ and $V$, and the unknown quantum state $|\psiangle$.
main_assumptions: The core assumption tested is the equality between the input description (LHS) and the required output structure (RHS) of the proposed deleting machine.
paper_structure: The paper builds upon prior work on identical copies, defines the non-identical unitary copies ($U|\psiangle$ and $V|\psiangle$), proposes a specific deletion operator, and then rigorously proves its impossibility through algebraic manipulation.
why_interesting: This work extends fundamental no-cloning theorems into the realm of distinguishing between different types of quantum state redundancy (unitary vs. identical copies), which has implications for quantum error correction protocols and information processing limits.
